main_text.p: ab initiis obscurè co potentia creverunt, ut vix credenda patraverint. فالذي فعلوة في الاسلام لم يفعله احد قبلهم ولا بعدهم من المسلمين وملكوا كثيرا من بلاد العراق والحجاز وبلاد الشرق والشام الي باب مصر Fecerunt in Islamismo quod nec ante, nec post eos fecit e Moslemis quisquam, & occuparunt magnam partem regionum Eraki & Hejazi, nec non regionum Orientis & Syriæ usque ad portam Mesri, sive Cairo. Exorti sunt circa annum H. 278.

محمد بن جابر بن سنان الحراني [?] الاصل البتاني AlEattanius Mohammed Ebn Jaber Ebn Senan, origine AlHarrani (seu Harranensis) AlBattani, vel juxta alios AlBeitani, patriam scil. habens بتان [?] qui locus quidam est in ditione Harrani, Astronomus insignis, vulgò AlBategnius, observationes suas anno H. 264. inceptas, continuavit ad annum 306. obiit an. 317.

AlFarabius [al. طرخان] ابو نصر محمد بن ترخان الفارابي Abu Nasr Mohammed Ebn Tarchan AlPharabi, patriam scil. habens فاراب Farab Turcarum urbem, quæ postea Otrar dicta, quæ eadem AlJauharii (ut diximus) patria, الجوهري Philosophorum apud Mohammedanos facile princeps, simulque ازهد الناس في الدنيا mundi contemptor egregius, verè Philosophus. Mortuus est anno H. 339. plusquam octogenarius. Ebn Chal. AbulF. &c.
p.122.Sharifob Edrisi شريف الادريسي [?] Sharifol Adrisi q.d. Illustrü

page.notes: Arabic lines transcribed letter by letter from a small, slightly skewed scan; doubtful Arabic words are marked [?], especially the nisba and place-name readings in the AlEattanius entry and the Arabic name Edrisi. The Latin "Syriæ" and "Illustrü" are uncertain at the line ends. The left-margin "p.122." is a printed reference beside the last paragraph. The ending "Illustrü" runs on at the foot of the page; the text is not a catchword since it stands on the last line. The bottom-left corner shows a dark shadow and the right edge shows a neighbouring page edge, which are not transcribed.
